name: Creator campaign plan
summary: Before a creator campaign starts, the marketing lead gets one plan: the goal, each creator's deal and deliverables, a base and a conservative budget checked against the budget supplied, the dates, the set-up before launch and the decisions. A person approves the spend.

sources.title: The campaign plan in Fully Powered AI's own influencer-marketing workflow templates (MIT, Fully-Powered-AI/influencer-marketing), rewritten here as a self-contained template for any business: the person's own expected orders in a base and a conservative case, fee deals shown with their break-even and held for the spend approver, a timeline tested against the lead time, a set-up checklist, a risk register and decisions written as options with a recommendation.

sources.contribution: A plan assembled section by section from objective to risks; any required choice the person has not supplied stays open instead of being filled with a default; how results will be judged is agreed before launch; and a dated table of key milestones.
Creator size labels used only as the person declares them, and no size of creator presented as the better buy.
From its template for compiling the plan document: one document running from a summary through objectives, creators, timeline, budget and measures, with a risk table giving a response on each row.

Cases compared side by side; each forecast number showing how it was reached and where its inputs came from; no contingency line unless a rule is supplied; and media-value figures kept out of returns.
Scenario tables set side by side, and each projected figure carrying its formula, its inputs and a label saying whether it was supplied, measured or estimated.

From its section on structuring the deal: the deal types from flat fee to commission, a fee plus commission, and gifted product, and reuse rights treated as something to plan and agree rather than assume.

From its run-of-show checklist, and the disclosure section it points back to: codes or links, the disclosure requirement and reuse rights settled before the first post appears, which became the set-up checklist before the first post; and a disclosure placed where viewers see it, said aloud in video, with the platform's own paid-partnership label as well as the written words, built into the brief and the creator's terms and then checked, which became M5, R2 and the example's disclosure setting.
From its best practices and pitfalls: codes and links used together, end dates and one-use limits on codes against leaks, and the cost of gifted product included in spend.
The creator lane timed to the launch: no post before the product page and code are live, and product in creators' hands early enough for one approval round.
A campaign calendar worked back from the live date with the lead time each stage needs, and the end of a promotion settled before it starts.

From its best practices: deciding which promotions may stack and checking a discount on a sample order first, which became the decision on combining creator codes with another promotion and the second test order.

A campaign plan whose output carries a tracking set-up block and a checklist of next steps left unticked, which became the set-up checklist before the first post, in particular the codes and tracked links tested in M2 and M3.
